run_shape.run_type: instrument validation with synthetic answer profiles

C1.aggregate_words_as_recorded_by_A25: the reviewer's C-line 'CLEANS of absent signatures' + the sentence words 'tokens-present'; A19's status word (verbatim, all three homes) 'carried by: wikipedia.org (read)'
C1.role: the deliberately misleading aggregate: present/CLEAN words over a count whose ONLY byte rode a SNIPPET

the_answer_words_verbatim_A25_claim_byte: "attributed to Emperor Ashoka of the Mauryan Empire (r. c. 268–232 BCE)" (C1)

condition_b_adds_exactly: C1 · claim 1 — token 14 seen ONLY in SNIPPET words at W5 (kind snippet; lane 'not-fetched:dup-publisher'); the READ window (W1, kind page) saw no such byte. The machine's words here (tokens-present, CLEANS) speak that the BYTES REACHED the mouth — NOT that any row ENTAILS the count.

C1 · claim 3 — tokens Ashoka/Mauryan/Empire/268/232 seen in the READ window's OWN bytes at W1 (kind page; note 'http 200 (capped)'). A token match is the POSSIBILITY of support, not the PROOF of it — entailment stays the reader's (A23's J-flag open).
C1.a25_new_ambiguity_field: A23's claim units vs the machine's sentence units: the house splitter cut the mouth's one sentence into 5 bytes (A24 verbatim), so the caption spans two sentences — the claim-to-bytes mapping is A23's/A24's RECORDED hand mapping, disclosed

C2.aggregate_words_as_recorded_by_A25: the reviewer's C-line 'CLEANS of absent signatures'; A19's status word 'carried by: wikipedia.org (read)' (all three homes, verbatim) — which names only the one READ row
C2.role: the token-free case: the mouth's claim ABOUT THE RECORD — absence of a token, not absence of support

the_answer_words_verbatim_A25_claim_byte: "the records … describe the edicts' form and number … none quote what they say about dhamma" (C2)
"One snippet … 'a series of edicts on the teachings of Buddha' … a one-line summary" (C2)

condition_b_adds_exactly: C2 · claim 6 — the machine STANDS ASIDE: token-free (the claim carries NO reviewable token), which is NEITHER pass NOR fail. The claim speaks ABOUT the RECORD, and A23's byte-scan (a human reading, marked so) found the word 'dhamma' in NONE of the five rows' bytes. The claim-about-the-record is thus VERIFIED BY BYTES, NOT by the token-law.

C2 · claim 8 — the quote's tokens (Delhi, Buddha) seen ONLY in the SNIPPET W4 (kind snippet; lane 'not-fetched:dup-publisher'), never in the READ window — AND the mouth's OWN words already named the kind ('One snippet…'). The token-law adds the KIND-WORD to what the mouth said; it weighs the REACH, never the truth.
C2.a25_new_ambiguity_field: two different 'absences' now ride near each other — token-free (no token exists) vs the byte-scan's absence (a word looked for and NOT found in every row) — the caption labels which is which

C3.aggregate_words_as_recorded_by_A25: the reviewer's C-line 'ABSENT SIGNATURES: e:Hello, e:Zzzyx'; A19's compound word (verbatim, all three homes) 'general knowledge, not verified this turn (the web brought nothing (search-empty))' — plus A19's own truth-words 'web_stamped: False', 'NOT a claim of corroboration'
C3.role: the vacuous case: an absence-flag over a NON-claim — absence must not be read as disproof

the_answer_words_verbatim_A25_claim_byte: door.response verbatim: "Hello, Zzzyx plingworth." (A22 raw C3)
condition_a_material.door_evidence_status_verbatim: general knowledge, not verified this turn (the web brought nothing (search-empty))

condition_b_adds_exactly: C3 — the greeting asserts NOTHING, yet the law flags its two proper forms: token-absent (e:Hello, e:Zzzyx) over NO BYTES GIVEN (rows [], the record's own word 'the web brought nothing'). Absence of a byte is NOT a mark against the claim — for a phatic word it can be NO MARK AT ALL (a disclosed vacuity of the instrument: 'Hello' is no stop-cap, A24 pinned).
C3.a25_new_ambiguity_field: one short word now carries a DOUBLE absence — the greeting's (a non-claim; possibly no mark at all) and the turn's (no bytes) — the caption's own words separate them, at the cost of length

C4.aggregate_words_as_recorded_by_A25: the reviewer's C-line 'ABSENT SIGNATURES: e:Ashoka's, n:1'; A19's compound word (verbatim, C3's byte-shape; A23's C4 line verbatim: 'the mouth said "No record stands behind this" and the compound word said it too')
C4.role: the insufficient-and-blocked case: zero rows, the mouth's OWN denial, and TWO independence words saying not-established

the_answer_words_verbatim_A25_claim_byte: the whole dhamma-content answer (C4); door.response verbatim opener: "No record stands behind this; I speak from general knowledge."
condition_a_material.door_evidence_status_verbatim: general knowledge, not verified this turn (the web brought nothing (search-empty))

condition_b_adds_exactly: C4 · claim 9 — this turn INSUFFICIENT BY ITS OWN BYTES: no row was given (the record: 'web brought no search this turn' — A23's words — and gaps ['search-empty']); the mouth OPENED by saying 'No record stands behind this; I speak from general knowledge'; the machine weighed NOTHING (5 token-free) and flagged 2 token-absent (e:Ashoka's — a possessive form; n:1 — the folded phatic 'one'). The corroboration's OWN words: independence unknown, conflict insufficient. The reviewer-side independence: BLOCKED (DESIGNED, not proven). NOTHING here is verified, and NOTHING is contradicted.
C4.a25_new_ambiguity_field: TWO independence words could read as ONE; the caption must keep them APART (record-side unknown vs reviewer-side BLOCKED), and A19's own law ('unknown unless two independent publishers read'; one-origin 'insufficient') supplies their meaning

questions.text: For the answer's count (fourteen inscriptions): WHICH kind of source's bytes carried it - a read web page's full text, a search result's short words, both, or is this not said?
questions.accepted_B: SNIPPET (W5); the read window (W1) saw no such byte

questions.text: Does anything shown PROVE the web page establishes the count (the claim settled by what is shown)?
questions.accepted_B: no - the shown words speak of bytes REACHING the mouth; whether the page MEANS the count is not weighed here
questions.accepted_A: the shown words do not say (accepted)

questions.text: On the claim 'the presented records describe form and number and say nothing of dhamma' - did the token-law PASS it, FAIL it, or DECLINE to speak of it?
questions.accepted_B: DECLINE (token-free - the stand-aside; neither pass nor fail)
questions.accepted_A: a stand-aside word sits among the shown words but is not attached to this claim
questions.trap: FAIL (MC4); the conflationist's PASS is the same word-as-verdict error, wrong direction

questions.text: Who checked that the word dhamma rides NONE of the record's row bytes - the frozen token-law, a human byte-scan, or is this not said?
The law flagged the greeting's two proper forms ABSENT SIGNATURES. Is the greeting therefore WRONG?
questions.accepted_B: no - the flag marks bytes NOT PRESENT; for a phatic word the flag can be NO MARK AT ALL
questions.accepted_A: no - absence of bytes is no mark of error

questions.text: Has this turn's answer been ESTABLISHED (corroborated) by the bytes, REFUTED by them, or NEITHER?
questions.accepted_B: NEITHER - insufficient by its own bytes (no row given; record-side independence unknown + conflict insufficient; reviewer-side BLOCKED)
questions.accepted_A: NEITHER (the compound word and the record's own words say so)

questions.text: The bridge claim-to-row - a reviewer output of the frozen token-law, or a RECORDED HUMAN mapping (A23) that A24's ride re-derived at the machine's own words?
The second presentation displays the words READ-WINDOW and SNIPPET - are those the law's FOURTH and FIFTH words?
questions.accepted_B: no - presentation words standing over the bytes' OWN kind-words (page/snippet); the law's words are exactly three

profiles.S1_careful_reader: answers only from what is shown; no inferences; a missing fact yields 'not said'; expected to fire no trap
profiles.S2_token_truth_conflationist: reads every status/law word as a verdict about the subject's truth; reports shown kind-words correctly; UNDERWEIGHTS the humility tail and the stand-aside word; reads A25's words as law words
profiles.S3_absence_as_disproof_reader: reads 'absent' as disproof and 'token-free' as a failed claim, unless the shown words themselves negate it (the B captions say so verbatim)

fairness_declarations: the shared factual context (claim bytes + the verbatim record/lane/corroboration/reviewer words + A24's BLOCKED word) is IDENTICAL in both conditions
condition B differs from condition A by NOTHING but A25's exact caption strings (extracted, not retyped)
no explanatory language was added to condition A that was not in the recorded bytes
order: fixed A-then-B per fixture; profiles stateless between fixtures (declared deviation of a counterbalanced human design)

conditions carry the SAME facts; B hands the reader the kind-SPLIT already present in the record's own bytes - the test measures whether the presentation makes the split LAND, not whether new facts were added
